To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Na,K- ATPase has a physiological function in addition to being an enzyme that pumps Na(+) andK(+), namely to regulate the activity of the enzyme by binding to endogenous cardiotonics, and that this regulatory activity is conserved from yeast to mammals.
the Na,K-APase ouabain-binding sites are important for the normal physiological function of the Na,K-pump and for the regulation of blood pressure.

1) the ouabain binding site of the Na(+), K(+)-ATPase functions as a receptor that is activated by endogenous cardiotronic steroid-like compounds, and 2) the physiological significance of this site is that it regulates the activity of the Na,K pump in the brain, heart, kidney, and other tissues.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of the physiological significance of the ouabain binding site on the Na,K- ATPase.
the physiological role of the ouabain binding site of the Na, K-ATPase in normal and diseased states.
the role of the ouabain binding site in regulating the function of the Na,K pump and its role in the pathogenesis of hypertension and congestive heart failure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the physiological role of the ouabain-sensitive Na,K-ATpase site is still unknown.
the ouabain/Na,K-ATPases receptor function is not essential for life but is required for normal cardiovascular homeostasis.
the physiological function of the Na,K pump is not to generate a transmembrane Na(+) gradient, but rather to generate an intracellular K(+) gradient that is used by the cell for other purposes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Na,K- ATPase is a "two-faced" enzyme, with a "pump" face that is involved in the regulation of cellular Na(+) and a "receptor" face that is regulated by cardiotonic steroid hormones.
the ouabain binding site of the Na, K-ATPase has an important physiological function.
the ouabain receptor function of the Na,K pump has a significant role in normal physiology, but that this function may not be the sole role of the ouabain binding site.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Na,K-APase has an endogenous regulatory function in the cardiovascular system, but the physiological relevance of this function has not yet been fully elucidated.
the Na,K- ATPase has a receptor function and that it is a key player in the regulation of blood pressure.
the Na,K- ATPase has a physiological role in addition to its well-established role as a pump.
